cohort: Eighty-six pregnant women diagnosed with pregnancy-induced hypertension were included, divided into groups with raised or normal serum LDH levels.
finding: Elevated serum LDH alone in pregnancy-induced hypertension is not considered a prognostic indicator for maternal and neonatal adverse outcomes, with the exception of HELLP syndrome.
mod_finding: The study found no significant difference in the mode of delivery (cesarean section) between the groups with raised versus normal serum LDH levels.
